# sesh GUI — Master Feature→UI Map

The complete mapping of every sesh CLI/daemon feature to its graphical-app surface, with the chat-architecture and packaging verdicts and a consolidated build order.

---

## 1. Architecture

**The app is an API client, not a reimplementation.** sesh's daemon already exposes its *complete* router two ways (the same `d.routes()` mux behind both): a local **unix socket** (no auth, local trust) and an opt-in **TCP API** (`SESH_API_ADDR` + `Authorization: Bearer <SESH_API_TOKEN>`, refuses to bind without a token). The Svelte UI talks to **one daemon at a time**; cross-machine views (`--all-machines`, `mesh`, ticket `find`/`move`) are **fanned out daemon-side** over the peer mesh, so a client pointed at one daemon already sees and can act on the whole mesh. The GUI mirrors the existing TUI's design principle: it is a **thin client** that *emits verbs* (which auto-route to the owning daemon) and refreshes from the snapshot/mesh endpoints — it never reimplements a verb or invents state.

**The GUI replaces tmux as the client.** The entire `tmux nav/attach/switch-client` layer — addressing a process as `(machine, socket, session, window, pane)` and switching the attached terminal to it — collapses into **app selection state**: select a thread → its chat/terminal surface fills the main pane. Master-tmux cockpit commands (`master up/window/attach/down/ensure/watchers`) are a terminal-era stand-in for what the GUI *is*, and become non-features (kept only as an optional desktop power surface).

**The two chat modes (the central design fact).** sesh has **no unified "message" abstraction** — a thread is one of two runtime shapes, and the UI must branch per-thread on the two state axes (`head: headful|headless`, `busy: bool`) carried on every snapshot/grid row:

- **Headless thread** (no pane) → a clean request/reply shape: `send-headless` starts a background `<agent> --print/--resume` turn (returns immediately), the UI polls `headless-reply` for `working`/`have_reply`/`reply`, durable history is the on-disk transcript. **This is the principled, mobile-perfect chat path.**
- **Headful thread** (live tmux pane) → the conversation lives *inside* an interactive agent TUI the daemon does **not** drive turn-by-turn. `thread send` does `send-keys` (bracketed-paste for multi-line) into the pane; **there is no reply API** — the only readbacks are `thread capture` (raw pane screen-scrape) and the agent's own per-agent JSONL transcript (`transcript`/`tail`). `busy` in either case disables/queues the composer ("turn in flight", matching the daemon's 409s).

A hard cross-cutting fact: **there is no streaming/push channel anywhere today.** Every live view is poll-based. This is the single biggest sharp edge and recurs in every group's risks.

## 2. Screen map

| Screen | Primary content | Features that live here |
|---|---|---|
| **Threads grid (home)** | Virtualized, tree-structured live list of threads; the app shell. Backed by `GET /v1/mesh`. | `thread grid`/`list`/`snapshot`/`mesh`; state glyphs (head/busy/descendant/attach); columns + per-column color; cwd-label; parent/child tree; fuzzy filter; views/tab cycle; per-machine freshness strip; all row actions (new, resume, stop, delete, archive, rename, tag, reparent, notify, copy-id). The TUI feature floor. |
| **Thread detail / chat** | Master/detail (desktop) or pushed full-screen (Android). The reason the GUI exists. | `thread info`/`status`/`pane` (header/inspector); the **chat composer** (`thread send` / `send-headless` + `headless-reply`); **transcript** render (JSONL→bubbles) + **capture** "Terminal" tab; `await` (completion signal); blob attach (drag/paste/picker); `thread fork` (inline per-message branch); per-thread Tickets panel; `meta` advanced table; `delegate` reply surfaces as a one-shot bubble. |
| **Tickets board** | Kanban (status columns × ticket cards) + ticket detail/editor. | `ticket create`/`list`/`list-all`/`get`/`set`/`set-status`/`delete`/`send-prompt`/`needs-input`/`unbind`/`move`/`find`; blob tokens in prompts. |
| **Machines / mesh** | Machine sidebar (desktop) / picker (Android); per-machine reachability + freshness; **Advanced → tmux** diagnostics. | `peer add`/`list`/`remove`; `mesh`; `tmux info`/`create-session`/`kill-session`/`create-pane`/`send-text` (advanced); `thread adopt` (work-server pane picker); `master *` (optional cockpit panel); `master watchers` (drop/niche). |
| **Automation center** | Hooks table + subscriptions panel/graph. | `hooks list`/`enable`/`disable`/`test`; `subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`subscriptions`; the notify gate (`thread notify`). |
| **Settings / health** | Daemon health card per machine; diagnostics; data tools; onboarding. | `daemon status`/`restart`/`stop`; `doctor`; `backup`/`restore`/`copy`; `import` (v1 migration); token+endpoint config; column/theme/editor prefs. |
| **Notifications** (cross-cutting, Android-prime) | OS push / toasts. | Driven by `await`/`headless-reply` busy→idle edges + the `notify` gate + `ticket needs-input`. |

**Navigation primitives.** Clicking/tapping a thread row = "open" (the GUI's nav; auto-resumes a dead thread / promotes a headless one). `tmux nav --last` maps to a **Back / previous-thread** affordance backed by the *app's own* navigation history — **not** sesh's `nav-prev` file (that's shared cockpit state; desktop/Android/TUI must not fight over one cursor). None of the literal nav flags (`--in-client`, `--attach`, `--client`, carrier env, `SESH_NAV_CLIENT`) surface — they are tmux-client-identity plumbing with no GUI meaning.

| **doctor** | `GET /v1/doctor` → `{Checks[]{Name,Status,Detail}}` | Diagnostics panel: "Run diagnostics" → check rows (✓/!/✗ + detail + fix), summary banner, per-machine tabbed | Desktop multi-machine; Android local default | On-demand, "last run at" | P1 |
| **info** | composite (`ThreadList`+`ThreadStatus`+`TicketList`); no `/info` endpoint | Thread Detail/inspector (= the chat header): record + head/busy/attachment+clients + tmux locator + created + tags + tickets | Desktop side inspector; Android expandable header→sheet | head/busy/attachment live ~1–3s | P0 |
| **backup** | **CLI-only** — `ThreadList` + reads transcripts off **local disk**, writes SQLite | Settings→Data "Back up" (native file-save) / per-thread `⋯`; toast w/ written/unchanged/missing. **Electron-only** (shell out / link library) | Desktop only; hide Android | One-shot | P2 |
| **restore** | **CLI-only** — reads backup SQLite, writes transcripts; pi/codex `--native` Unsupported (loud) | Settings→Data "Restore" (file picker, to-dir/native, force, rewrite-cwd); surface Unsupported list loudly. Electron-only | Desktop only; hide Android | One-shot | P2 |
| **copy** | mostly CLI-orchestrated (`ThreadList`+backup; cross-machine = `stage-file --to` then routed `restore`); claude-only cross-machine | Per-thread `⋯`→"Copy transcript": to-folder (any agent) / to-machine (peer picker, claude-only, disabled-with-tooltip). Electron-orchestrated | Desktop only v1 | One-shot; cross-machine spinner | P2 |
| **fork** (`thread new --fork-from`) | `POST /v1/threads{fork_from,message_id}` → new headless thread (owner-only) | "Fork from here": thread-`⋯`→modal (name + turn-slider, default whole) **and** inline "branch from this message" in the transcript → new headless child w/ parent link | Both can fork; Desktop rich slider+inline; Android "fork whole" + name modal | One-shot; child via grid | thread-level **P1**; per-message **P1→P2** |

## 4. The two deep-dive verdicts

### 4.1 Chat architecture verdict

Four options were weighed against fidelity, latency, mobile fit, daemon-additions, **detach-safety** (the user is often personally attached to the same tmux session in their real terminal — the chat UI must never detach/resize/steal that client; `capture-pane`/`send-keys` are passive and safe, `attach`/`-CC` open a new client and must be sized/isolated), and multi-viewer cost:

- **(A) Headless turns + transcript polling** — `send-headless` + `headless-reply`/`transcript?tail=N`. High chat-semantic fidelity (clean user/assistant pairs, dedup on the monotone reply count), turn-granular latency, **mobile-perfect**, zero new endpoints, perfect detach-safety, trivial multi-viewer. Only valid when no live pane (409s otherwise).
- **(B) capture-pane polling + send-keys** — render `capture?lines=N` on a timer, type via `send`. Medium fidelity (an 80×24 screen, not messages; needs `-e`/ANSI to keep color), polling-bound latency, **perfectly detach-safe**, trivial/stateless multi-viewer. The pragmatic "watch + nudge a live thread" view.
- **(C) WebSocket pty bridge → xterm.js** — a new endpoint pumping a `tmux attach` pty over WS. Maximum fidelity, real-time, **significant daemon work** (WS upgrade, pty, resize, auth, cross-machine `ssh -tt`), and the **hard detach-safety problem** (must use a *grouped session* with explicit per-client sizing so we never resize the user, and closing the WS kills only our client). Desktop-first; Android poor.
- **(D) tmux control mode (`-CC`)** — structured `%output`/`%layout` event stream. High+structured, real-time, **largest** build (control-mode parser, brittle across tmux versions), same grouped-client concerns. Over-engineered for v1.

**Verdict — v1: A + B, no new transport.**
- **Idle/headless threads → (A)** as the primary message-bubble chat surface (transcript timeline + `send-headless` + busy-driven "working…"). Honest, clean, mobile-perfect, ships against existing endpoints.
- **Live-pane threads → (B)** as a read-mostly live view (poll `capture` with `-e`/diff, one-line `send` nudges) + a prominent **"Open terminal"** escalation to (C) on desktop, and a **"Stop & chat"** action that `stop`s the pane and flips the thread into the (A) model (the unified runtime model makes the same conversation resume seamlessly).
- **End-state: add (C)** the WS pty bridge as the "enter the live agent" experience — desktop-first, Android read-only/deferred, grouped-session + per-client sizing for detach-safety. Consider (D) only if multi-pane/layout awareness becomes necessary.

**New daemon endpoints for a materially better v1** (SSE — simpler than WS, works in Electron and Android `fetch`/EventSource):
- `GET /v1/threads/chat/stream?id=` (**SSE**) — watches the owner-side transcript / busy→idle edges + reply count, pushes `{role,text,replyCount}` as turns complete; replaces polling `headless-reply`/`transcript`; cross-machine over the existing peer transport.
- `GET /v1/threads/screen/stream?id=&ansi=1` (**SSE**) — daemon-side capture-pane diffs on a timer (so viewers don't each hammer tmux); backed by `CapturePaneLines` + `-e`.
- End-state: `GET /v1/threads/terminal?id=` (**WebSocket**, bearer-auth) — detach-safe grouped pty, bidirectional, `{resize,cols,rows}` control.
- A true token-level streaming chat needs the agents run in `--output-format stream-json` and deltas relayed — a *third* future endpoint, not v1.

**Chat risks:** detach-safety of any live attach is the top risk (a grouped/second client resizing the user's real panes is the exact "looks-fine-but-wrong" failure the project forbids — needs a dedicated proving experiment). v1 "live feel" is turn-granular not token-granular. capture-pane needs `-e`+a JS ANSI parser to look right. Per-agent JSONL transcript parsing (claude/pi/codex differ) is the heaviest, highest-correctness-risk renderer task — needs a typed parser per `agentKind` with a raw fallback. Composer routing (`send` vs `send-headless`) depends on fresh `head`/`busy` — mitigate with optimistic send → catch 409 → re-fetch axes → re-route. `headless-reply` is in-memory (lost on daemon restart) — reconcile against the durable transcript. EventSource can't set headers in browsers — a real constraint on the SSE token-auth choice (query-param token or WS).

### 4.2 Packaging / transport / auth verdict

The daemon exposes the full router over a local **unix socket** (no auth, local trust) and an opt-in **TCP API** (bearer `SESH_API_TOKEN`, refuses to bind tokenless, same mux = full parity). One client talks to one daemon; cross-machine is fanned out daemon-side. **No CORS, no SSE/WS** today; the Obsidian plugin dodges CORS via a native HTTP shim (`requestUrl`).

**Desktop (Electron):**
- Run a **local daemon** and reach it through the **Electron main process over the unix socket** via a typed `ipcRenderer.invoke('sesh', {method,path,body})` bridge (main process does `http.request({socketPath})`). The **renderer must never `fetch` the socket or hold a token** — inherits no-token local trust. **P0 path.**
- A **remote/headless desktop daemon** uses the same main-process proxy against the peer's **TCP API over tailscale**, token held only in the main process (OS keychain via `safeStorage`), never in the renderer/localStorage. **P1.**
- **node-pty terminal bridge** (xterm.js + node-pty in main) to `tmux attach` a pane — the one capability Android can't match. **P1** (chat-via-API is the P0 baseline).
- Renderer rule: one `seshClient` module with a transport seam (`ipc` local vs `tcp` remote); Svelte stores never know which.

**Android:**
- No local daemon — talk to a **remote always-on hub daemon over tailscale TCP** (e.g. `mymain:7878`) via a **native HTTP layer** (Capacitor/Tauri-native or Kotlin bridge), **not** WebView `fetch` (the daemon sends no CORS headers → blocked). Token in **Android Keystore/EncryptedSharedPreferences**. Because reads/routing fan out daemon-side, the phone pointed at the hub sees and acts on the whole mesh. **Configurable primary + fallback endpoint** (reuse the Obsidian `local`/`fallback` pattern). **P0 for Android existence.**
- **Offline**: phone is useless when the hub is unreachable — mitigate with a read-only **last-snapshot cache** (mesh/grid JSON) rendering stale-but-visible with a loud staleness banner; all writes require connectivity and fail loudly. **P1.**

**Cross-cutting:** **Keep dodging CORS** — route all traffic through a non-browser HTTP layer (Electron main proxy / Android native HTTP); the daemon needs no CORS changes and the wire stays identical to the CLI. Adding permissive CORS would be a security regression for a token-only service — flag to Lukas, don't add `Access-Control-*` silently. Freshness is poll today (~1–3s focused, ~3–5s list). Token provisioning = paste token+endpoint once (QR/paste), keychain-stored; no rotation endpoint (manual, by design).

**Transport risks:** the **no-push channel** is the dominant risk for chat (and `headless-reply` is in-memory/volatile) — likely needs the new SSE/WS endpoint above (a sesh-side addition, surface to Lukas). Electron renderer must never hold the token. Android shell choice (Capacitor vs Tauri-mobile vs Kotlin) must use native HTTP from day one or silently hit CORS. **Hub selection/failover** is an app concept the daemon doesn't model — needs an explicit endpoint-picker UX and a loud "hub asleep" state (not a silent retry that looks like an empty list). node-pty binds Electron to the daemon's host (cross-machine pty = the same `ssh -t` the cockpit uses — defer). The shared long-lived bearer token has no per-device issue/revocation — a lost phone means rotating the token on every daemon.

> **The peers-registry GUI gap (recurs in two groups):** `peer add/list/remove`, `master watchers`, and backup/restore/copy are **CLI-only** (mutate a local `peers.json` / read local transcript files). Electron can touch the file/binary directly; **Android cannot**. Decision needed: add `/v1/peers` CRUD endpoints (cleanest — unblocks mobile + remote management) vs. file-only desktop management. Same for whether backup/restore are in v1 scope at all or punted to "run the CLI".

---

## 5. Consolidated build order

### P0 — the spine (an app you can chat with)
- **Transport+auth foundation**: Electron main-process socket proxy (renderer never holds a token); Android native-HTTP hub client (Keystore token, primary+fallback endpoint). The `seshClient` transport seam.
- **Mesh model + Threads grid (home)**: poll `GET /v1/mesh` → virtualized tree of thread cards; head/busy/descendant/attach glyph cluster (faithful 1:1 of the `ThreadRow` fields incl. `?`-unknown — the prime directive); per-machine freshness strip (offline = visibly dimmed last-known, never silently stale); fuzzy filter; active/archived/all tab cycle; parent/child tree.
- **Thread detail + chat**: detail header (`info`/`status`); the chat composer routing `thread send` (headful) / `send-headless` (headless) off fresh `head`/`busy`; transcript JSONL→bubbles renderer (per-`agentKind`); capture "Terminal" tab for live panes; `await`/`headless-reply` busy→idle "turn running…"/done signal.
- **Lifecycle from the grid**: new, resume/headful (unified **"Open"**), stop, delete (confirm), with loud persistent action errors separate from the live-poll model.
- **Multi-machine basics**: peer list (machine sidebar/switcher) + **peer add**; mesh freshness.
- **Tickets core**: board (`list-all`), create, get, set, set-status (drag + bind), send-prompt; needs-input "!" badge.
- **Blobs core**: blob add (attach/paste/drop → `@blob`) + blob get (thumbnails/preview).
- **delegate** (quick-ask) and **notify** gate (push knob).
- **Daemon status/health pill**; **thread info** inspector.

### P1 — the full cockpit
- thread list (pickers), archive/unarchive, rename, tag (+remove), reparent (drag-drop + persistent error), status/pane refinements.
- transcript "load earlier" paging; capture interactive embed (desktop).
- Tickets: find (deep-link), delete, unbind, move, needs-input source decision; blob expand (pre-send lint).
- Automation Center: hooks list/enable/disable; subscriptions view + subscribe/unsubscribe.
- Machines: peer remove; doctor diagnostics; remote-daemon restart.
- fork (thread-level + inline per-message branch); stage-file attach (P0 if images-in-prompts is a v1 must).
- Columns picker + cwd-label + custom views; daemon restart.
- Android: offline last-snapshot cache; notify→push wiring.

### P2 — power & hygiene
- Advanced→tmux panel (info tree, create-session, kill-session + "clean up empty"), thread adopt (pane picker), meta table, raw send-text.
- master cockpit panel (up/down/ensure/attach embedded terminal); drop master watchers/current.
- hooks test; subscriptions graph; ticket import (internal).
- backup/restore/copy (Electron-only); v1 import; blob ls/rm/path; per-column colors; copy-id; refresh.
- **End-state**: SSE chat/screen streams; WS pty terminal bridge.

### Top risks (ranked)
1. **No push/streaming channel** — the whole API is poll + a volatile in-memory `headless-reply`. A responsive chat (and Android push) likely needs a new SSE/WS endpoint; surface to Lukas before committing to poll-only.
2. **Detach-safety of any live terminal attach** — a grouped/second tmux client must never resize/steal the user's real attachment or kill the wrong client. Needs a dedicated proving experiment before (C) ships. The exact "looks-fine-but-wrong" failure the project forbids.
3. **Per-agent JSONL transcript parsing** (claude/pi/codex differ, raw lines) — heaviest renderer work and top correctness risk; needs typed parsers + raw fallback.
4. **Glyph/state honesty** — head/busy/descendant/attach badges must be a faithful 1:1 of the `ThreadRow` fields (`?`-unknown rendered distinctly), and offline machines must render visibly offline with dimmed last-known data. The prime directive applies to the GUI.
5. **CORS / token boundary** — keep dodging CORS via non-browser HTTP; Electron renderer must never hold the token; Android must use native HTTP from day one or silently fail.
6. **Peers-registry + backup/restore/copy are CLI/file-only** — Android can't reach them; decide on `/v1/peers` CRUD and whether backup/restore are v1.
7. **Hidden cross-machine `move` on ticket bind** — must be visible (progress + active→ready rebind) with loud error paths, or users are confused.
8. **Inline base64 blob upload** (no multipart/streaming) — large Android camera images bloat client+daemon memory and may hit body limits; define a downscale policy or add a streaming upload endpoint.
9. **Per-verb routing differs** (subscribe→subscribee's owner; delegate→whole-verb `--machine`; await→mesh-agnostic; stage-file/blob→thread's machine) — a single global "machine" dropdown will misroute; encode the right target per action.
10. **`~`/cwd portability** — folder/box pickers must emit owner-relative `~` paths, not bake in the local home (a known past bug), or cross-machine spawns point nowhere.
